article_title: Building a Well-Qualified Transitional Kindergarten Workforce in California: Needs and Opportunities
citation: Melnick, H., García, E., & Leung-Gagné, M. (2022). Building a well-qualified transitional kindergarten workforce in California: Needs and opportunities. Learning Policy Institute. https://doi.org/10.54300/826.674
title: Candidate pools and credentialing pathways for building the TK teaching workforce
description: The report identifies four pools of potential TK teacher candidates: current Multiple Subject credential holders who can teach while earning 24 ECE units; early childhood educators with a bachelor's degree, for whom "possible pathways this group might take to a credential include teacher residencies, postbaccalaureate credentialing programs, and internship programs"; early educators without a bachelor's degree, suited to apprenticeship and degree pathway programs; and new candidates for assistant positions, including recent high school graduates and career changers, buildable through dual enrollment pathways. Table 4 and Figure 6 map these pools to pathways.
requirements: Lead TK teachers must hold a Multiple Subject Teaching Credential plus, by August 2023, 24 units of ECE coursework, a Child Development Teacher Permit, or equivalent experience
Assistant TK teachers need a high school degree and a basic-skills/pedagogical-knowledge assessment
constraints: New candidates without credentials would not fill lead TK teacher positions in the short term
The state does not currently have data on the number of TK teachers employed by districts
target_learners: high school students in dual enrollment
target_learning_goals: bachelor's degree attainment for early educators
examples: LEAs can organize and fund cohorts of teachers to take ECE-focused coursework at partner universities
Integrated teacher education programs allow candidates to earn a bachelor's degree and teaching credential in 4 years building on community college coursework
key_sources: Melnick, H., García, E., & Leung-Gagné, M. (2022). Building a well-qualified transitional kindergarten workforce in California: Needs and opportunities. Learning Policy Institute. https://doi.org/10.54300/826.674

article_title: A Systematic Review of Teachers’ Knowledge of Self-Regulated Learning and its Assessment
citation: Yves Karlen · Charlotte Dignath. (2026). A Systematic Review of Teachers' Knowledge of Self-Regulated Learning and its Assessment. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10171-2
title: TK-SRL framework: three interrelated dimensions of teachers' knowledge of self-regulated learning
description: The Teacher Knowledge of SRL (TK-SRL) framework adapts Shulman's teacher knowledge theory to SRL, distinguishing three interrelated dimensions: "content knowledge of SRL (CK-SRL), pedagogical content knowledge for promoting SRL (PCK-SRL), and assessment knowledge for diagnosing SRL (AK-SRL)". CK-SRL covers phases, components, and conditional strategy knowledge; PCK-SRL covers direct promotion and indirect activation of SRL; AK-SRL covers diagnosing largely non-observable regulatory processes. General pedagogical knowledge is deliberately excluded as non-SRL-specific. The framework served as an a priori lens for coding the 33 included studies.
requirements: Teachers need knowledge of regulatory phases (forethought, performance, reflection) and of cognitive, metacognitive, motivational, emotional, and resource-oriented components
AK-SRL requires interpreting indirect indicators of learning rather than solely observable products
constraints: The framework does not directly address teachers' beliefs, motivational orientations, or learning environments; it focuses on the knowledge component only
target_learning_goals: understanding and promoting students' self-regulated learning
examples: The review illustrates the three dimensions with a writing-task scenario in which CK-SRL identifies regulatory difficulties, AK-SRL gathers diagnostic evidence via learning diaries and observations, and PCK-SRL translates the diagnosis into modeled planning strategies and scaffolded reflection
key_sources: Yves Karlen · Charlotte Dignath. (2026). A Systematic Review of Teachers' Knowledge of Self-Regulated Learning and its Assessment. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10171-2

article_title: Enhancing Transfer of Knowledge in Physics through Effective Teaching Strategies
citation: Akinbobola, Akinyemi Olufunminiyi. (2015). Enhancing Transfer of Knowledge in Physics through Effective Teaching Strategies. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.6, No.16. https://www.iiste.org
title: Transfer of Knowledge Test in Physics (TKTP), a 50-item multiple-choice transfer measure
description: The Transfer of Knowledge Test in Physics (TKTP) is a researcher-made instrument of 50 multiple-choice items on sound energy and light energy, each with four options and one correct answer, used to measure students' ability to extend what was learned about heat energy to new concepts. It was face and content validated by four physics teachers and trial tested with 50 subjects outside the main sample. The article reports that "TKTP has a reliability coefficient of 0.76" using Kuder-Richardson formula 21, with average difficulty and discrimination indices of 60.62 and 0.52.
requirements: Content validity by subject teachers and trial testing to establish reliability before main use
constraints: Designed for the heat-to-sound/light transfer context in Nigerian senior secondary physics
target_learning_goals: transfer of knowledge across physics concepts
examples: Pretest scores on the TKTP were used as covariate measures in the ANCOVA to account for pre-existing ability differences between groups
key_sources: Akinbobola, Akinyemi Olufunminiyi. (2015). Enhancing Transfer of Knowledge in Physics through Effective Teaching Strategies. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.6, No.16. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1079935
